name: glm53-qual-v1
purpose: Long-context qualification: 591 IDs (559-token prompt of eight unrelated passages plus 32 teacher-forced continuation IDs) from QUALIFICATION_TEXT in crates/qwen-llm/src/glm5_next_metal/tests.rs. Serial logits validate native long-context decode; batched logits give llama.cpp's own batched-vs-serial envelope for the Fast packed lineage.
token_source: tokens.txt in the location below; the test re-tokenizes QUALIFICATION_TEXT and asserts every oracle record's token matches

producer.device: Apple M4 Max 128 GB, Metal, all layers offloaded

serial.bin.run: logits only, n_batch = n_ubatch = 1, all 591 positions

batch.bin.run: --batch: one llama_decode over all 591 IDs, logits at every row

observations: llama.cpp batched vs its own serial decode: KL 8.6e-3 at the prompt end (position 558), 4.2e-2 worst, mean 2.6e-3, 16 top-1 flips at reference margins up to 0.34.

Native serial vs serial.bin: KL <= 1.1e-9 through position 155, top-1 at all 591 positions. At position 156, block 27's 8th and 9th biased router scores tie exactly (gap 0 in llama.cpp F32). Native keeps the lower expert id (9); llama.cpp's bitonic argsort keeps 115. That position spikes to KL 4.9e-3, later blocks route differently on the changed hidden state, and later positions keep a median offset around 3e-8.

Native Fast packed prefill vs native Exact (= serial): KL 5.6e-3 at the prompt end, 9.1e-3 worst over 33 steps, top-1 flips only at reference margins <= 0.06. Chunks 512 and 128 are bitwise identical, as are 64 and 97.
